title: Model-Contrastive Federated Learning
layout_note: One input photo stack on the left fans out by orthogonal arrows into three stacked copies of the model (previous local, current global, current local); their outputs converge on a loss box at the right.
grouping: Each model copy is a dashed blue rectangle titled above or below (local model t-1, global model t, local model t). The loss is a dashed rectangle titled local loss holding two smaller dashed boxes joined by a bold black plus. A solid-outline legend box top right maps the three bar colours to layer roles. The input is a dashed rectangle labelled party i.
shapes_depth: Flat. Each model is three tall thin vertical bars side by side - red, blue, yellow - with dark outlines, one bar per layer group; the three copies are identical, so only their titles tell them apart. Arrows are thin blue orthogonal lines; the contrastive loss is fed from the middle (blue) bar of each copy, the supervised loss from the last (yellow) bar of the current local model. Serif labels, no math.
proposed_highlight: No special colour for the new loss; it is listed first inside the loss box, and the figure's structure (three versions of the same network fed the same input) carries the idea. Round indices t-1 and t in the box titles make the comparison across rounds explicit.
lesson: Draw one client's network three times - previous local, current global, current local - as identical colour-coded layer stacks titled with their round index, so the loss reads as a comparison between versions of the same model.
notes: Venue from the arXiv comment (Accepted by CVPR 2021).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: federated image classification with model-contrastive local loss

core.what: three identical three-bar model copies stacked in a column (local model t-1, global model t, local model t) receive the same party image, and lines from their middle projection-head bars converge on one 'model-contrastive loss' box at the right

relations.form: lines from the blue projection-head bar of each of the three copies run down and right in parallel into the top 'model-contrastive loss' box of the dashed 'local loss' frame
the three copies are drawn as identical dashed boxes of red, blue and yellow bars, stacked vertically and captioned by time and role, so they compare layer by layer
one party's photo stack at the left fans three elbow arrows into the three model copies
the local model t's yellow output-layer bar sends one arrow into 'supervised learning loss', joined to the contrastive loss by a bold plus inside the local-loss frame

channels.colour: bar fill = layer role (red base encoder, blue projection head, yellow output layer), keyed in a legend at the top right; blue = all arrows
channels.shape: vertical bars = network parts; photo = local data; text boxes = loss terms
channels.line: solid blue arrows = data / representation flow, one style throughout
channels.frame: dashed box = one model copy, the party's data, or the local loss

quality.strengths: the contrastive comparison is between model copies, and the figure draws exactly that: three identical bar glyphs at three times, with the compared layer (projection head) wired into the loss; the losses are named and joined by a visible plus
quality.weaknesses: the representations themselves (the projection-head outputs) are not drawn as nouns - wires go straight from bars to the loss box, so which pair is positive and which negative is not shown; the three projection-head wires run as a tight bundle of parallel elbows that are hard to tell apart; the legend box takes the top-right corner for three swatches

insights.structure: Three dashed-box model copies stacked vertically in the middle (local model t-1 top, global model t middle, local model t bottom), the party's photo stack on the left, a dashed 'local loss' box on the right, and a colour legend top-right.
insights.data: Each model is three coloured vertical bars (red base encoder, blue projection head, yellow output layer) so the three copies are visually identical and comparable layer by layer.
insights.emphasis: The losses are named in the right box as 'model-contrastive loss' plus 'supervised learning loss' joined by a bold plus sign, and the contrastive loss is fed from the projection-head bars of all three models.
insights.flow: Left to right: the input image fans out to three models; the projection-head outputs of the three models run down/right into the model-contrastive loss, while only the local model t's output layer feeds the supervised loss.
insights.avoid: The representation arrows from the top two models cross through the middle model box and overlap, making it hard to trace which head feeds which loss.

arrangement.units: three dashed-border boxes, one per model copy, each holding three coloured layer bars
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo stack labelled 'party i' in a dashed frame
arrangement.shared: the same input fans out to all three models; the colour code for layers is shared
